paragraphs: Swansea Council's fostering service is Foster Wales Swansea, one of the 22 council fostering services that together make up Foster Wales, and the independent agencies shown above also cover the city. When a Swansea child needs a foster home the council's fostering team asks its own carers first and approaches agencies only when none of them is free. Its own figures for 2023-24 show 141 children placed in foster care, 30 of them with agency carers; of those 30, fourteen were in sibling groups, four were in parent and child placements, five were over 13 and seven were younger children with complex needs.

Those figures show where more local carers are wanted: brothers and sisters who need to stay together, parents who need support with a baby, teenagers and children with complex needs. Across Wales, Foster Wales reports around 4,875 children in foster care in March 2024 and 2,042 children needing a foster carer between April 2023 and March 2024, with council carers looking after around 74% of new placements.

In February 2025 the Senedd passed a law that removes private profit from children's residential and foster care in Wales, so in future that care will be provided only by public, charitable or not-for-profit organisations. If you are comparing services, ask each one how this affects them.

Foster Wales Swansea sets out seven steps: an enquiry, a home visit, a free two-day Skills to Foster course, an assessment with checks and references, a fostering panel and a decision usually within one to two weeks of panel, then matching. It says the whole process typically takes around four to six months, and that renting or owning your home, and being single or in a relationship, make no difference. You need a spare bedroom.

The council says its fees and allowances are above the Welsh Government minimum, with extra payments for birthdays, Christmas and holidays and a weekly fee while approved carers wait to be matched. Carers have a dedicated supervising social worker, a support line outside office hours, support groups including one for carers' own children, a buddy scheme and free training, at least 15 hours a year. Speak to the council and two or three of the services above, and see the Wales page and the Neath Port Talbot, Carmarthenshire and Bridgend pages for services nearby.
